messages:
mariya: Heads-up — spotted a new latency regression during last night's traffic ramp. p95 for short prompts (<= 16 tokens) jumped from ~42ms to ~110ms on the g4-pool around 02:14 UTC. Looks correlated with a very high prefix-cache hit rate.

alex: can you paste the perf traces / a short profile? is this steady-state or a spike?

mariya: steady for ~20m, then recovered. attaching clipped profiler sample: ```
# pprof top (service=g4-infer)
Count  Time  Function
1200   38ms  kernel_dispatch_small_seq
950    30ms  batch_slot_manager::admit
800    25ms  kv_cache::lookup
...```

jun: quick hypothesis: when many requests are cache-hit, virtual_length seen by batcher drops -> chooser picks the "tiny-seq" kernel which is cheaper per-op but has much worse throughput at high qps due to kernel launch overhead. That and microbatch churn = many 1-2 item batches.

sara: +1. we've seen this pattern before but usually at extreme hit rates. What are the batch formation stats?

mariya: grabbed recent batcher debug lines: ```
[02:13:40] batch formed: slots=1 tokens=3 virtlen=2 latency=6ms
[02:13:40] batch formed: slots=1 tokens=2 virtlen=1 latency=7ms
[02:13:41] batch formed: slots=2 tokens=4 virtlen=2 latency=9ms
[02:13:42] admission: token_budget=32 min_fill=0.2 -> admitted 1/8
```

alex: so admission is too permissive when prefixes hit: token_budget is per-batcher-target (32) but most reqs are 1-2 tokens after prefix, so we end up sending many tiny microbatches. Two levers: increase min_fill by tokens not fraction, or add a hit-streak-based boost to target_token_budget.

jun: another angle: kernel chooser threshold. Current rule: if virtlen <= 8 -> tiny_kernel. We could change to consider "eff_batch_size" estimate (virtlen * estimated_batch_slots) instead of raw virtlen. If estimated batch_slots>4 then prefer wide kernel.

sara: I propose a small canary: (1) change admission to require min_tokens=4 when hit_rate>0.6 for 5m window; (2) chooser change to use eff_batch_size heuristic; (3) keep both behind flags. Run on g4-pool-canary.

mariya: I've run a local sim with recent traffic trace and the min_tokens=4 rule reduced microbatch count by 70% and lowered p95 in sim to 48ms. But throughput dropped ~3% in the sim workload when hit_rate dips.

alex: acceptable trade if we gate by hit_rate. Also add fallback: if queue depth grows > 1500, revert.

jun: small config prototype (for ops): ```json
{"batcher": {"min_tokens_on_hit": 4, "hit_rate_window_sec": 300, "hit_rate_threshold": 0.6}, "chooser": {"eff_size_threshold": 16}}
```

perf-bot: Uploaded flamegraph: https://perf.redwood.internal/fg/2305006789. Shows kernel_dispatch_small_seq hot path and heavy kernel startup times. :mag:

sara: action items: mariya -> deploy canary config to g4-pool-canary and leave for 2h during a spike window; jun -> add eff_batch_size calc and flag; alex -> add short-circuit revert if queue backlog or error rate rises; perf-bot -> run automated comparison baseline for p50/p95/p99.

mariya: I'll schedule canary for 04:00 UTC and post results in this thread. Also attaching a short script to extract hit_rate and virtlen histograms: ```bash
curl -s $BATCHER/debug | jq '.metrics | {hit_rate: .prefix_hit_rate, virtlen_histo: .virtlen_hist}' > /tmp/scan.json
```

alex: nice. also let's add a transient metric "microbatch_churn" (#batches with slots<=2 / total_batches) so we can alert.

jun: one more note — kernel microbench that prompted tiny_kernel adoption used synthetic single-threaded runs; need a production microbench using realistic batch_slot distributions. filed a card.

sara: OK. if canary looks good we'll roll with a 6-hour gradual rollout with the revert guard. :thumbsup:

mariya: thanks everyone. I'll post the canary log and perf bot diffs after 06:30 UTC.

alex: thanks — appreciate the quick triage :rocket:
